concept_a: nimodipine dosing (60mg q4h for vasospasm prophylaxis after SAH)
concept_b: methylprednisolone NASCIS dosing (30mg/kg bolus for acute spinal cord injury)
disambiguation_axis: indication and drug class — calcium channel blocker (SAH) vs corticosteroid (SCI); NASCIS protocol now largely abandoned
volume status — CSW is hypovolemic hyponatremia (treat with isotonic/hypertonic fluids); SIADH is euvolemic/hypervolemic (treat with fluid restriction; opposite treatment

concept_b: MAP target (varies by diagnosis — ~80-90 in TBI, <140 in ICH)
disambiguation_axis: CPP is the goal (perfusion); MAP is the controllable input to achieve it; 60 belongs to CPP not MAP

concept_b: rebleed risk window (highest in first 24h after SAH, especially first 6h)
disambiguation_axis: timing and mechanism — rebleed = re-rupture of aneurysm (early); vasospasm = smooth muscle contraction from blood products (delayed)

concept_a: Cushing reflex (hypertension as compensatory response to rising ICP)
concept_b: primary hypertension (independent elevated MAP not driven by ICP)
disambiguation_axis: causality — Cushing is BP rising TO protect CPP; treat ICP first. Primary HTN is the primary problem; treat MAP directly

concept_a: uncal herniation (lateral transtentorial — compresses CN III and contralateral peduncle)
concept_b: central transtentorial herniation (downward displacement of diencephalon through tentorial notch)
disambiguation_axis: direction and structures — uncal = lateral mass effect, CN III palsy first; central = symmetric downward, Cheyne-Stokes breathing first

concept_a: epidural hematoma CT appearance (biconvex/lenticular hyperdense collection, does not cross sutures)
concept_b: subdural hematoma CT appearance (crescent-shaped hyperdense collection, crosses sutures, follows brain contour)
disambiguation_axis: shape and suture crossing — biconvex = EDH (limited by sutures); crescent = SDH (crosses sutures freely)

concept_a: anterior cord syndrome (motor loss + pain/temp loss; preserved proprioception/vibration)
concept_b: central cord syndrome (upper extremity > lower extremity weakness; bladder dysfunction; most common incomplete injury)
disambiguation_axis: which tracts are spared — anterior = dorsal columns spared (proprioception OK); central = peripherally located tracts spared (legs better than arms)

concept_a: Fisher grade (CT grading of subarachnoid blood volume — grades 1-4)
concept_b: Hunt-Hess grade (clinical grading of SAH severity based on neurological exam — grades 1-5)
disambiguation_axis: what is graded — Fisher = imaging (blood on CT); Hunt-Hess = clinical exam (LOC, headache, deficits)

concept_a: vasodilating antihypertensives worsen ICP in TBI (hydralazine, nitroprusside — cerebral arteriolar dilation increases CBV)
concept_b: nicardipine acceptable in ICH/SAH (autoregulation partially intact; benefit of BP reduction outweighs mild vasodilation)
disambiguation_axis: autoregulation status — TBI has lost autoregulation so vasodilation transmits directly to ICP; ICH/SAH have partial autoregulation buffering

concept_a: L4-L5 disc herniation (compresses L5 nerve root — foot drop, great toe extension weakness, dorsal foot numbness)
concept_b: L5-S1 disc herniation (compresses S1 nerve root — plantar flexion weakness, Achilles reflex loss, lateral foot/sole numbness)
disambiguation_axis: dermatomal and myotomal distribution — L5 = EHL, medial/dorsal foot; S1 = plantar flexion, Achilles reflex, lateral foot

concept_a: posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES — vasogenic edema from failed autoregulation, usually posterior cortex)
concept_b: hypertensive encephalopathy (diffuse cerebral edema from breakthrough hyperperfusion, not necessarily posterior)
disambiguation_axis: distribution and mechanism — PRES = preferentially posterior (less sympathetic innervation), predominantly white matter; hypertensive encephalopathy = diffuse

concept_a: GCS motor score (1-6 scale: 1=no response, 6=obeys commands — component of total GCS 3-15)
concept_b: modified Rankin scale (0-6 scale: 0=no symptoms, 6=death — functional outcome measure used post-stroke or post-op)
disambiguation_axis: timing and purpose — GCS is real-time acute consciousness assessment; mRS is functional outcome at days-weeks post-event

concept_a: ventriculoperitoneal shunt (VP shunt — CSF diverted to peritoneum; first-line for most hydrocephalus)
concept_b: ventriculoatrial shunt (VA shunt — CSF diverted to right atrium; used when peritoneum is contraindicated)
disambiguation_axis: distal limb destination and indications — VP = peritoneum (default); VA = atrium (abdominal adhesions, peritonitis, prior failed VP)

concept_a: diabetes insipidus (DI — deficient ADH, produces large volumes dilute urine, hypernatremia)
concept_b: cerebral salt wasting (CSW — natriuresis with volume depletion, hyponatremia)
disambiguation_axis: serum sodium — DI = hypernatremia + dilute urine (Na >145); CSW = hyponatremia + concentrated urine with high urine Na
